questions.question: P alone can complete a piece of work in 15 days and Q alone in 20 days. P and Q undertake to do the work for ₹ 4,500. With the help of R, they complete the work in 6 days. How much should be paid to R?
questions.questionHtml: P alone can complete a piece of work in 15 days and Q alone in 20 days. P and Q undertake to do the work for ₹ 4,500. With the help of R, they complete the work in 6 days. How much should be paid to R?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM of 15 and 20 = 60 units

P = 60/15 = 4 units/day
Q = 60/20 = 3 units/day
P + Q + R = 60/6 = 10 units/day

R = 10 - 4 - 3 = 3 units/day

R’s 6 days work = 3 × 6 = 18 units

R’s share = 18/60 × 4500 = ₹1350

questions.question: Read the following passage and answer the given questions accordingly: The intellectual lineage of Ancient Greece reached its zenith through the triumvirate of Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle. Socrates, the foundational figure, operated on the premise that "the unexamined life is not worth living," employing a dialectic method to strip away false certainties. Unlike the Sophists who charged for wisdom, Socrates claimed to know nothing, viewing himself merely as a "midwife" to the ideas of others. His trial and subsequent execution for impiety and corrupting the youth marked a pivotal moment in Western thought, transforming him into a martyr for the cause of rational inquiry and moral integrity. Plato, Socrates' most illustrious student, preserved his mentor’s legacy while expanding into metaphysical realms. In his "Theory of Forms," Plato posited that the physical world is but a shadowy reflection of a higher, immutable reality of perfect ideas. Aristotle, however, shifted this focus back to the empirical world. As a student at Plato’s Academy, he eventually diverged from his teacher’s idealism to champion "Empiricism"—the belief that knowledge is derived from sensory experience and logical categorization. While Plato looked toward the heavens for truth, Aristotle looked toward the earth, laying the groundwork for modern scientific methodology. Q- According to the passage, what was the primary difference between Socrates and the Sophists?

questions.question: In the following question, one statement is given, followed by certain inferences. Consider the statement to be true even if it seems to contradict commonly known facts. Read the inferences carefully and decide which of them logically follows from the given statement. Statement: Machines can perform repetitive tasks faster and more accurately than humans. Inferences: I. Machines are more efficient than humans in repetitive tasks. II. Humans and machines differ in their capabilities.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, one statement is given, followed by certain inferences. Consider the statement to be true even if it seems to contradict commonly known facts. Read the inferences carefully and decide which of them logically follows from the given statement.

Statement:
Machines can perform repetitive tasks faster and more accurately than humans.

Inferences:
I. Machines are more efficient than humans in repetitive tasks.
II. Humans and machines differ in their capabilities.
questions.solution:
👉 Inference I:
Since machines are both faster and more accurate, they complete repetitive tasks better than humans. Efficiency means doing work in less time with better accuracy. Therefore, machines are more efficient in repetitive tasks.
✔ Inference I follows

👉 Inference II:
The statement compares humans and machines and shows that machines perform better in certain tasks. This clearly indicates that both do not have the same ability, i.e., there is a difference between them.
✔ Inference II follows

👉 Final Answer: Both I and II follow
